labeling.method: one human pass: 306 frames at 12s on contact sheets + independent Gemini transcript (21 x 3-min mono segments, per-segment drift rescaled); single speaker on stage with collage slides, Q&A from ~52:00; timing ~±5s

moments.note: Day one at EFF: crashing the Broadcast Flag meeting, suing the FCC and winning
The door to a good internet is open a crack, and the guy who unlocked it is Donald Trump; 'when life gives you SARS, make sarsaparilla'
Trump's coalition roll-call ending in libertarians with 'low-tax brainworms' who'd vote for Mussolini; laughter and applause
What anti-circumvention law actually criminalises; 'felony contempt of business model'
CAFTA story: 'they won't take our coffee unless we give them anti-circumvention' explains why every country caved
'We have tariffs now' - if they burn your house down anyway you can stop obeying; 'happy liberation day?'
Give Trump everything except Greenland - 'he'll take fucking Greenland'; 'like all the best Americans, I am Canadian'
Retaliatory tariffs are like punching yourself in the face and hoping the downstairs neighbour says ouch
Apple's 30% App Store tax ($100bn/yr): Finnish geeks with a jailbreak dongle could undercut it by 90%
'Your margin is my opportunity'; every pirate wants to be an admiral; 'move fast and break kings!' to applause
Grudging respect for the USTR; 'not an accelerationist, but not exactly not an accelerationist... is Trump a comrade?'
Apple pulls ICEBlock and classifies ICE officers as a protected class; technologists fleeing the US
'It beats the shit out of' burning hundreds of billions on AI data centres for defective chatbots; big applause
Microsoft cuts off the ICC's Outlook: 'in a he-said, Clippy-said... I know who I believe'
John Deere remotely bricks tractors looted from Ukraine - and could brick most tractors in the world
Digital sovereignty without migration tools is 'housing in East Berlin for people who live in West Berlin'; seize the means of computation
Free software as a commons, like structural engineering: no secrecy in the maths that keeps buildings - or pacemakers - up
'Software is not an asset, software is a liability' - commons-based production spreads the liability
Tech bosses 'horny' for chatbots that shit out code: tech debt at scale
The chatbot can't do your job but the AI salesman can convince your boss; bosses fear they hold a Fisher-Price steering wheel
Striking Hollywood writer: prompting AI is like studio notes - 'make me E.T. but about a dog' - minus being called an idiot suit
Zuckerberg's chatbot friends: for Zuck your friends are the problem - 'a social network with no social'
Billionaires are solipsists: Musk's NPCs, EA's imaginary humans, Trump's 'science without scientists' that won't tell him not to inject bleach
Energy crisis made the EU leap on solar; the balcony-solar objector can 'fold it until it's all corners' - applause
US consumption collapse: only so many Lambos and Sub-Zero freezers 'even the most guillotineable plute' can own
Dieselgate and German carmakers renting you your accelerator pedal and high beams; 'let me cook!'
Medtronic's parts-pairing ventilators during COVID lockdowns: 'It was lethal. It killed people.'
Newag bricks its own trains, sues the Dragon Sector hackers; 'won't someone think of the poor train saboteurs?'
Anti-circumvention made an 'enshittogenic environment' that ushered in the Enshittocene; time to seize the means of computation
Isn't it weird you must pick a network to talk to someone? '1985 called, and it wants its walled gardens back!'
After 24 years, the door is open a crack: 'not optimistic - fuck optimism'; hope is a discipline, don't despair
Q&A rules: one part, not a comment, 'almost without exception it's not about AI'
Non-technical people hack when it pays: the nursery worker with a two-SIM phone
Lawmakers needn't understand microbiology to give us safe tap water; 'technology is very interested in you'
